o: **Understanding the problem**: Find i < j < k with strictly increasing values maximizing `nums[i] − nums[j] + nums[k]`. For a fixed middle j, the best choice is the smallest value before j (as i) and the largest value after j (as k), provided both strict inequalities hold. Example 2: for j = 2 (value 3), prefix min is 1 and suffix max after is 6 → 1 − 3 + 6 = 4. With n up to 10⁵, an O(n²) triple loop is too slow; precomputed suffix maxima plus a running prefix min give O(n).
k: Decompose on the middle index j: answer = max over j of (prefixMin[j−1] − nums[j] + suffixMax[j+1]) when both inequalities hold.
Suffix maxima come from one backward pass; the prefix min is maintained on the fly in a forward pass.

a.i: Try all (i, j, k) and keep the best valid value. Direct translation of the statement; useful as a correctness baseline.
s: Triple nested loop i < j < k.
If nums[i] < nums[j] < nums[k], update the answer.
a.t: O(n³) — all triples examined (fine only for tiny inputs)

a.n: Approach 2: Suffix max + running prefix min
a.i: Precompute suffixMax[t] = max(nums[t..n-1]). Sweep j left to right keeping the minimum value seen strictly before j; whenever prefixMin < nums[j] < suffixMax[j+1], candidate = prefixMin − nums[j] + suffixMax[j+1]. Since a valid triplet is guaranteed, the answer is positive.
s: Build suffixMax in one backward pass.
Sweep j from 1 to n−2 maintaining prefixMin of nums[0..j−1].
If prefixMin < nums[j] < suffixMax[j+1], update the answer; then fold nums[j] into prefixMin.
a.t: O(n) — one backward pass for suffix maxima, one forward sweep
a.sp: O(n) — suffix-max array (reducible to O(1) with a cleverer single pass)

w: **Wrap-up**: Present the brute force only to establish the decomposition on j, then immediately give the O(n) sweep. Pitfalls: strict inequalities (equal neighbors disqualify), updating prefixMin **after** evaluating j, and integer overflow in Java/C++ (values up to 10⁹ make the expression exceed int). Follow-ups: maximize a weighted variant, or answer queries on subranges (then sparse tables for prefix/suffix extrema).
